1.mascotDialogue: A collision here isn't an error, güey — it's an outcome the whole design plans for! Each bucket just becomes a tiny linked list instead of one slot.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 13's the whole strategy — instead of overwriting whoever's already in the bucket, the new node just points at it and becomes the new head! Nothing's ever lost to a collision.

3.mascotDialogue: Bucket 3 now carries a two-node chain — 17, inserted after 10, lands at the head, exactly like insert-at-head says it would!

4.mascotDialogue: The chain looks perfectly fine — one node, no dangling pointer in sight. That's the trap! The bug isn't a broken pointer, it's a silently vanished one — and this app shows 'lost node' plain, so it never hides.
